Hi Olivia — appreciate the clear summary and the spec. Attaching a short note on how we typically compute and what carveouts look like on Hosted API. High-level answers below; I'm happy to turn any of these into contract text.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Measurement: we compute per-route latency on 1-minute buckets (wall-clock aligned) and maintain rolling histograms per bucket. Quantiles (p50/p95) are derived from the concatenated histogram across the measurement window. Default measurement window we use for SLA assessment is 24 hours expressed as 1440 x 1-minute buckets.
- Carveouts: we support two carveout classes — scheduled (customer-provided calendar entries) and transient outliers detected by traffic amplification heuristics. Scheduled carveouts are excluded from SLA calculations if provided 48h in advance.
- Outlier detection: our engine flags buckets where request rate > X * baseline (configurable; default X=6) for that route. Flagged buckets are cloaked from the quantile aggregation if they meet the configured spike-duration threshold (default 3 consecutive 1-minute buckets).

Differences from a plain rolling-window p95: instead of aggregating all raw latencies into a single long list (which is sensitive to rare long tails), we:
- maintain per-minute histograms to preserve temporal locality, then
- apply a trimming pass to remove flagged buckets (scheduled or transient) before computing the quantiles across the remaining histogram.

Why we like this approach:
- preserves short-timescale SLIs for debugging while preventing a handful of short, extreme bursts from dominating a daily p95;
- allows explicit scheduled carveouts for your batch windows;
- is deterministic and auditable — we store the list of excluded bucket timestamps and the trigger reason in the audit log attached to each SLA calculation.

If you'd prefer industry-standard alternatives, we can also provide:
- a fixed 1-hour sliding-window p95 sampled every 5m, or
- a trimmed-mean latency (e.g., 95th percentile after removing top/bottom 2% of samples).

I've attached a short explainer I wrote for our SREs (redwood-latency-binning.md) that shows pseudocode for detection thresholds and how the audit trail looks.

Proposed next steps:
1) Confirm that scheduled batch windows (name + recurrence + timezone) can be submitted by Fintegra and will be excluded if posted 48h in advance.
2) If you want transient carveouts, confirm the spike multiplier (we can default to 6x) and minimum consecutive minutes (we default to 3).
3) We'll draft contract wording and send a DocuSign when you approve.

Happy to hop on a 30-min sync next Tue 09:00-10:00 PT — does that work?

Subject: Internal: Fintegra carveout sizing / risk note

Markus / Karthik — internal note to capture risk and the range we can offer in the contract. Posting here so it's in-thread for legal and AM.

Risk assessment:
- If we allow very permissive carveouts (low multiplier, many scheduled windows), the effective p95 could drift and the SLA becomes less meaningful. We should limit scheduled carveouts to known recurring windows and a small monthly budget for ad-hoc carveouts.

Commercial options to offer: 
1) Default (no charge): scheduled carveouts up to 4x 30-minute windows per month + transient carveouts with multiplier=6x and min-duration=3m.
2) Premium (small fee): add 12x 30-minute scheduled carveouts per month and lower multiplier to 4x.
3) Contractual audit clause: all excluded buckets will be shared to Fintegra in the post-incident report; if Fintegra disputes excluded buckets, we will escalate to a joint review within 72h.

Suggested contract snippet (short):
"For the purpose of quantile-based latency SLOs (p50/p95), Redwood will compute quantiles from per-minute latency histograms across a 24-hour measurement window. Buckets identified as scheduled maintenance (submitted >=48 hours prior) and transient traffic amplifications (request rate >= 6x baseline for >=3 consecutive minutes) will be excluded from the quantile aggregation. Redwood will provide a timestamped audit log of excluded buckets upon request."

If we go with option 2 for Fintegra, we should price the addon as an annual line item tied to committed capacity.

— Monica
